source: Wicke (2024) Probing Language Models' Gesture Understanding for Enhanced Human-AI Interaction
finding: Project proposal to test whether text-only LLMs understand gestures given as text descriptions. It plans Turing-Experiment style replication of psycholinguistic studies.
numbers: Uses the Matsumoto and Hwang Verbal Message List: 96 items with gesture description, region and category. Models planned: Llama-2, OPT, Alpaca, GPT-NeoX, Bloom. No results reported.
quote: Currently, no interdisciplinary exploration exists into the role of gestures in the LLM context.
limits: It is a proposal only. The paper says no experiments were run and outcomes are unclear.
agent_relevance: Shows the gap: as of early 2024 there was no direct LLM test of gestures as thinking tools, only of gesture meaning.

source: Wicke (2024) Probing Language Models' Gesture Understanding for Enhanced Human-AI Interaction
finding: Cites earlier work (Wicke 2023) that LLM metaphor interpretation improved with the rated embodiment of the action words.
numbers: Correlation was positive. Exact coefficient not given in this paper.
limits: Second-hand report inside the proposal; not checked at the original.
agent_relevance: Weak hint that body-linked content is easier for LLMs; useful only as background.

source: Ghanad Torshizi, Hensel, Shapiro, Marsella (2025) Large Language Models for Virtual Human Gesture Selection
finding: GPT-4 picks co-speech gestures for a speaker. More prompt information (gesture-intent list, annotated examples) gave more appropriate and fewer inappropriate gestures than a bare prompt.
numbers: 2x2 prompt design (intents explained or not x examples given or not) on 20 test utterances from one labor-activist speech (21 training utterances, six minutes annotated video). Two experts rated jointly. Ordering reported: approach 3 > 1 and 2 > 0. Counts are only in figures.
limits: One speaker, 20 utterances, two raters who resolved disagreements together. No inter-rater statistic. Gesture meaning, not gesture as thinking aid.
agent_relevance: Prompting a model with a small closed set of image-schema gesture intents (path, container, cycle, collect) is a cheap way to constrain output. Scaffold lesson: closed vocabulary beats free choice.

source: Ghanad Torshizi, Hensel, Shapiro, Marsella (2025) Large Language Models for Virtual Human Gesture Selection
finding: Rheme and theme analysis by GPT-4 predicts when a human speaker gestures.
numbers: Of 49 speaker gestures, 43 fell inside the GPT-4-identified rheme and 6 outside (1 deictic, 2 beat, 3 metaphoric).
limits: One speaker. No baseline such as random placement.
agent_relevance: Supports the idea that gesture marks new information; timing can be predicted from text alone.

source: Ghanad Torshizi, Hensel, Shapiro, Marsella (2025) Large Language Models for Virtual Human Gesture Selection
finding: Latency of LLM gesture selection. Full output takes 6.5 to 9.3 seconds per utterance; a truncated query is near 1 to 2 seconds.
numbers: Per utterance mean 6.51 to 9.29 s across four approaches (approach 0 slowest, approach 1 fastest). Truncated query: GPT-4 1.20 s, GPT-4o-mini 1.08 s, Llama 3.1 1.23 s, fine-tuned Llama 2 7B 1.8 s. Target was under 1 s.
limits: Network latency, not compute. Not real time yet.
agent_relevance: Cost of adding a gesture-planning step is about 1 second even in short form.

source: Ghanad Torshizi, Hensel, Shapiro, Marsella (2025) Large Language Models for Virtual Human Gesture Selection
finding: LLMs store gesture knowledge by role. GPT-4 listed typical gestures for clinicians and politicians; the system maps them to a character animation engine.
numbers: Temperature 0.2, max tokens 256. Mentions an earlier study (Hensel et al.) where GPT-4 beat GPT-3 and GPT-3.5.
limits: Qualitative demonstration for the role part.
agent_relevance: Persona-linked gesture style is available by prompting.

source: Hensel, Yongsatianchot, Torshizi, Minucci, Marsella (2023) Large language models in textual analysis for gesture selection (ICMI)
finding: GPT-4 suggests gestures for a speech with minimal prompting and often finds novel but fitting ones.
numbers: On an Obama speech: 43.2% of suggestions similar to the true gesture; 43.2% different but judged appropriate; 13.5% inappropriate.
limits: Single speech, small sample, human appropriateness judgement. Justifications sound good but are not tested.
agent_relevance: Few-shot, low-annotation gesture planning works about as well as hand-built systems; errors are about 1 in 8.

source: Yerukola, Gabriel, Peng, Sap (2025) Mind the Gesture: Evaluating AI Sensitivity to Culturally Offensive Non-Verbal Gestures
finding: New dataset MC-SIGNS tests models on culture-specific gesture meaning. LLMs over-flag gestures as offensive.
numbers: 288 gesture-country pairs, 25 gestures, 85 countries. LLM recall 63 to 99% but specificity 1 to 61%. Gemma-2b 99% recall, 1% specificity. gpt-4o: 87% recall, 42% specificity. Llama-3.1-8B best balance, then GPT-4.
limits: Temperature 0. Dataset is small. Gesture knowledge tested as text labels.
agent_relevance: Gesture knowledge in LLMs is shallow and biased to one culture; do not rely on it for safety judgement.

source: Yerukola, Gabriel, Peng, Sap (2025) Mind the Gesture: Evaluating AI Sensitivity to Culturally Offensive Non-Verbal Gestures
finding: Text-to-image and vision-language models default to US meanings and miss non-US ones.
numbers: DALLE-3 rejects only 10.7% of offensive gesture requests. For universal concepts such as wishing luck, DALLE-3 misinterprets 84.1% of cases and gpt-4o 82.8%, giving locally inappropriate gestures. Adding scene context did not change LLMs but worsened T2I and VLM results.
limits: US-centric accuracy gap for all models. Some VLMs near chance.
agent_relevance: Models have a US-centric prior on gesture meaning, so any gesture channel in an agent needs locale checks.

source: Zeng et al. (2023/2024) GestureGPT: Toward Zero-Shot Free-Form Hand Gesture Understanding with Large Language Model Agents
finding: A multi-agent LLM loop (description agent, inference agent, context agent) maps free-form hand gestures to device functions with no training.
numbers: Zero-shot Top-1/Top-5: smart home (18 functions, AR headset) 44.79% / 83.59%; video streaming (66 functions, desktop) 37.50% / 73.44%.
limits: Offline validation. Gesture is first turned into text descriptions from hand landmarks, so the LLM never sees the movement.
agent_relevance: A working LLM agent loop that treats gesture as evidence to be reasoned about with context.

source: Zeng et al. (2023/2024) GestureGPT: Toward Zero-Shot Free-Form Hand Gesture Understanding with Large Language Model Agents
finding: Context ablation: gaze helps much more than history; all context together can hurt the top-5 list.
numbers: Smart home Top-1/Top-5: gaze only 35.16% / 83.59%; history and external only 23.18% / 49.48%; all context 44.79% top-1 but 79.69% top-5, below gaze only 83.59%.
limits: Authors say extra context sometimes misleads the agent, for example a mention of fingerprint unlock. Also a bias toward some functions.
agent_relevance: More context is not always better. A scaffold should select context, not dump it.

source: GIRAF authors (2023) GIRAF: Gesture-Informed Robot Assistance via Foundation Models
finding: An LLM planner that combines pointing gestures with language beats a language-only baseline for robot table-top tasks.
numbers: User study: more than 70% higher success rate than language-only. GestureInstruct set with 36 task scenarios: 81% correct plans (zero or few shot).
limits: Handles static gestures only. Dynamic gestures were shown in reasoning but no robust detector exists.
agent_relevance: Pointing replaces long verbal description; the same gain is a reason to let an agent use deixis-like references (marks, ids) instead of prose.

source: Hu, Ma et al. (2025) GesPrompt: Leveraging Co-Speech Gestures to Augment LLM-Based Interaction in Virtual Reality (DIS)
finding: Adding co-speech gestures to speech lets users give spatial instructions to an LLM copilot faster and with less prompt effort.
numbers: 12 participants. Mean task time: GesPrompt 43.65 s (SD 15.55), gesture-only 91.11 s (SD 23.00), voice-only 108.58 s (SD 29.46). SUS: 86 vs 74 vs 59.
limits: N=12, mostly young men, within-subject, small lab tasks. Speed tests communication, not thinking.
agent_relevance: Gesture carries spatial information that words carry badly; this is the communicative side, not the cognitive-tool side.

source: Hu, Ma et al. (2025) GesPrompt: Leveraging Co-Speech Gestures to Augment LLM-Based Interaction in Virtual Reality (DIS)
finding: Gesture shape matters for accuracy in the path task.
numbers: Path similarity: line 95.25% (SD 2.34), circle 90.67% (SD 3.45), sine wave 88.50% (SD 7.37). Free-hand pointing error 12.54% vs reference 18.18%.
limits: Small N. Differences between shapes tested within the same 12 users.
agent_relevance: Simpler spatial primitives are read more reliably.

source: Ram, Suresh, Saberpour Abadian, Demberg, Steimle (2025) GestureCoach (UIST)
finding: Fine-tuned model predicts which phrases in speaker notes deserve a gesture; it beats off-the-shelf LLMs at this.
numbers: Held-out F1 about 21.9. Rating study N=30; rehearsal study N=10 with significantly more gesture diversity. Spans up to 3 words.
limits: F1 is low, authors argue gesture placement is one-to-many. Tiny N for the rehearsal study. Trained on TED gesture patterns.
agent_relevance: Models find where emphasis goes, but exact placement is loosely defined.

source: Pang et al. (2024) LLM Gesticulator: LLMs for scalable and controllable co-speech gesture synthesis
finding: First LLM backbone for audio-driven full-body gesture generation. Quality scales with model size and text prompts control style.
numbers: Scaling shown across model sizes on BEAT (figure 7); smaller models repeat sequences and run too long. Outperforms prior work on objective metrics and a user study.
limits: No single headline number in the text I read. Beat-alignment scores did not correlate with human-likeness ratings.
agent_relevance: Scaling holds for gesture motion; but gesture here is output, not a reasoning aid.

source: SARGes authors (2025) SARGes: Semantically Aligned Reliable Gesture Generation via Intent Chain
finding: Intent-chain prompting makes an LLM decompose speech into gesture labels; a small model distils it.
numbers: Qwen1.5-1.8B partial overlap 50.2%; Qwen2-0.5B 42.4%; slightly below GPT-4. GPT-4 took about 3 s and about 8,000 tokens per set; the small model 0.4 s.
limits: Overlap is a lenient metric. Ethogram built by the authors.
agent_relevance: Chain-of-reasoning prompt distilled into a small model: a pattern for cheap gesture-like planning steps.

source: Gao et al. (2023) GesGPT: Speech Gesture Synthesis With Text Parsing from ChatGPT
finding: ChatGPT is used as an intent classifier plus emphasis-word finder; a lexicon of professional and base gestures is merged.
numbers: Tested on BEAT (English) and ZHUBO (Chinese). Semantic scores near ground truth on BEAT; the gap to baselines larger on ZHUBO.
limits: Metrics are proxies. ZHUBO has weaker pose estimation. No effect sizes extracted.
agent_relevance: Early evidence LLM text parsing adds semantic signal for gesture output.

source: Understanding Co-speech Gestures in-the-wild (JEGAL, Oxford VGG, 2025)
finding: A tri-modal gesture-speech-text embedding learned from videos beats large vision-language models on three gesture tasks.
numbers: Ablation: phrase loss only R@5 12.20, R@10 23.60; word loss only 8.50 / 14.60; both 18.80 / 30.80. Spotting accuracy 63.60 (both) vs 20.83 and 52.46. Speaker detection 48.0%. Concat fusion 18.8 R@5 vs average fusion 17.0.
limits: Gallery of 500 clips; absolute recall is low. Weak supervision from web video.
agent_relevance: Current VLMs are weak at reading gesture meaning from video; trained encoders do better.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought Elicits Spatial Reasoning
finding: Telling GPT-4 to 'Visualize the state after each reasoning step' improves spatial tasks. This is the closest LLM analogue of an external spatial thinking aid.
numbers: GPT-4 VoT vs CoT vs no-viz vs GPT-4V CoT. Route planning success rate 14.72 vs 9.48, 10.28, 5.65; next-step prediction 55.28 vs 48.61, 48.49, 46.59; visual tiling 63.94 vs 54.15, 46.98, 49.62; natural-language navigation 59.00 vs 54.00 CoT and 35.50 no-viz (+23.5 over no-viz).
quote: Visualize the state after each reasoning step.
limits: Gain over CoT in text navigation not significant (p<0.16). Still far from perfect. Not a gesture study; analogy only.
agent_relevance: Prompt: Visualize the state after each reasoning step. Cheap to add as a scaffold step for spatial problems.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought Elicits Spatial Reasoning
finding: Visualizations are often wrong, and VoT can hurt where logic alone suffices.
numbers: Visualization compliance with spatial constraints 51 to 52%; state visualization accuracy 24 to 26%; correct decisions 65 to 77% when the visualization was accurate. In the ring-navigation task, where the task reduces to modular arithmetic, VoT underperformed.
limits: Two tasks measured. Limits are task-type specific.
agent_relevance: Use external spatial tools only when the task is spatial; verify what is drawn.

source: Li et al. (2025) Imagine while Reasoning in Space: Multimodal Visualization-of-Thought
finding: Letting a multimodal model generate images as intermediate thoughts beats text-only CoT on maze, MiniBehavior and FrozenLake tasks.
numbers: Direct about 70% accuracy; GPT-4o worse with or without CoT; MVoT over 90% on Maze and MiniBehavior, +7% over Direct on FrozenLake; over 20% above CoT in the hardest cases. Built on Chameleon-7B with a token discrepancy loss.
limits: Trained model, synthetic grid worlds. Image quality limits results.
agent_relevance: Closest published test of 'think in drawn images' for models; supports external depiction as a reasoning aid.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Visual Sketchpad: Sketching as a Visual Chain of Thought for Multimodal Language Models
finding: Giving a multimodal LM drawing tools (lines, boxes, marks, zoom) improves math and vision tasks; no training needed.
numbers: Average gain 12.7% on math and 8.6% on vision tasks; geometry average gain 11.2%. GPT-4o with Sketchpad: V*Bench 80.3%, BLINK spatial reasoning 83.9%, visual correspondence 80.8%.
limits: Needs a multimodal model and tool code. Benefit varies by task.
agent_relevance: A drawn mark is an agent-side analogue of a gesturing hand: an external action that offloads spatial thought. Directly usable in an agent loop.

source: Synthesis across c01-c27: no study tests the gesture-helps-the-gesturer-think claim in LLMs
finding: Every machine study found uses gesture as communication or as output to render (selection, timing, recognition, safety). None tests whether producing a gesture improves the model's own reasoning. Spatial-tool papers (VoT, MVoT, Sketchpad) are the nearest analogue.
numbers: Counts: 12 gesture-specific LLM papers read; 3 spatial-externalisation papers read; 0 direct tests of Pouw-style gesture-as-cognition.
limits: Based on arXiv searches only (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate-limited). Absence may reflect search limits.
agent_relevance: Gesture is background only for the schema. If anything is borrowed, borrow externalised spatial marks (VoT, Sketchpad), not gestures.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Visual Sketchpad (second result set)
finding: Sketchpad also adds specialist vision tools (segmentation, depth) inside the same loop; drawing is an action, not an image generator.
numbers: Vision tasks span depth, spatial reasoning, jigsaw, visual and semantic correspondence, MMVP and V*Bench; gains shown on all seven types; math average gain with GPT-4o 11.2% on geometry.
limits: Gains differ by task. Needs tool-calling and a multimodal base model.
agent_relevance: Design pattern for an agent: let the model act on the problem with marks, then re-read the marks.

source: Li et al. (2025) MVoT (failure side)
finding: MVoT quality depends on image fidelity. Without the token discrepancy loss, generated visuals show redundant patterns and wrong content, hurting accuracy.
numbers: Authors report the loss reduces redundant patterns and inaccurate visual thought; GPT-4o with or without CoT stays below the roughly 70% Direct baseline on these tasks.
limits: Ablation numbers not extracted here. Synthetic tasks only.
agent_relevance: If an agent draws, a wrong drawing misleads it; verify drawings.

source: Wu et al. (2024) VoT (model comparison)
finding: Text-only GPT-4 with a 2D grid and VoT outperforms GPT-4V given the image with CoT on spatial tasks.
numbers: Route planning success 14.72 (VoT) vs 5.65 (GPT-4V CoT); visual tiling 63.94 vs 49.62; next-step prediction 55.28 vs 46.59.
limits: GPT-4V was an early vision model; later models may differ.
agent_relevance: Writing the state out as symbols can beat looking at a picture.
